stories.title: Klay Thompson Signs With Miami Heat — Tier 1

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
OFFICIAL: Klay Thompson signs 2-year, $13M deal with the Miami Heat.

Four titles. Five All-Stars. Now joining Giannis and Bam in South Beach.

Miami's new Big Three era just leveled up. 🔥

#HeatNation #NBA

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Klay Thompson didn't retire. He went to Miami.

Four championships, a career-worst season in Dallas, and now a chance to chase No. 5 next to Giannis.

South Beach gets serious. 🌴

#NBA #HeatNation

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

Klay Thompson is headed to Miami. 🌴🏀

The Dallas Mavericks bought out the final year of his contract — a deal worth $17.5 million for 2026-27 — and Thompson has now signed a two-year, nearly $13 million deal with the Miami Heat.

Think about what Miami just assembled: Giannis Antetokounmpo. Bam Adebayo. And now Klay Thompson — a four-time NBA champion and five-time All-Star who brings more championship experience than almost anyone in the league.

Yes, last season was a career-worst for Klay: 11.7 points per game on 39.3% shooting in Dallas. But Miami didn't need him to be the Klay of 2016 or 2019. They needed a proven floor-spacer with championship DNA, a guy who knows how to play in big moments without the ball.

The Heat lost Tyler Herro and Norman Powell this offseason. Klay steps in as the veteran sharpshooter who keeps defenses honest while Giannis and Bam operate in the paint.

He's 36 years old, still competing, still chasing rings. Championship No. 5 has a new home base: South Beach.

What do you think — is Klay the missing piece for Miami? 👇

stories.title: Kawhi Leonard Case Could Create League-Wide Salary-Cap Loophole — Tier 1

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
The Kawhi investigation just got bigger.

Forbes warns the NBA ruling could create a league-wide cap loophole — affecting EVERY team, not just the Clippers.

If sponsor introductions become a gray area, the CBA changes forever. 👀

#NBA #Clippers

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
The Kawhi Leonard case isn't just about the Clippers.

It could give EVERY team a loophole to funnel money through sponsorship deals.

Resolution expected ~September 22.

#NBA #Clippers

facebook.long_form:
Window: 11:00 AM ET

The Kawhi Leonard investigation just became everyone's problem.

We've been following this story for weeks — the Clippers under investigation for allegedly funneling money to Leonard through inflated sponsorship deals (a $28 million arrangement with Aspiration and a separate deal with Daktronics, the scoreboard maker at Intuit Dome).

Now Forbes is raising a flag that few people are talking about:

Whatever the NBA rules here could create a league-wide precedent.

If the league says teams can introduce players to sponsors — and those sponsors pay players above market rates — where's the line? Could every team in the NBA start using "sponsor introductions" as a quiet workaround to the salary cap?

The Clippers call it common practice. The NBA says the deals were significantly above fair market value. The NBAPA and Steve Ballmer are both preparing legal challenges if the ruling restricts these introductions.

The Board of Governors meets in mid-September. Resolution is expected around September 22. And when a decision finally comes, it won't just affect the Clippers or the Kawhi Leonard trade.

It might change how every front office does business.

Stay tuned. This one matters. 👀

stories.title: LeBron James Confirms 24th Season at Fanatics Fest NYC — Tier 2

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
LeBron James almost didn't come back.

At Fanatics Fest NYC, he said joining the 76ers was his "last decision" — and retirement was a real option.

24th season. Philadelphia. One more run. 👑

#76ers #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

LeBron James almost walked away.

At Fanatics Fest NYC this weekend, LeBron sat down for a live podcast with Tyrese Haliburton and got real: signing with the Philadelphia 76ers was his "last decision" — and retirement was genuinely on the table before he made it.

He's going back for a 24th NBA season. One more run. And he chose Philadelphia — a city and a team that needed a beacon after years of injury heartbreak.

Think about what the 76ers have now: Joel Embiid. Tyrese Maxey. Jaylen Brown. LeBron James. Their title odds went from 20-1 to 10-1 the moment LeBron announced.

LeBron said this would be his "last decision" — meaning his last time choosing where he plays. His career is now in its final chapter, and he wrote it in Philly.

At 41 years old, having played more playoff minutes than any human being in NBA history, he's still choosing to compete. Still showing up.

Whatever you think about GOAT debates, legacy debates, stat debates — the fact that he's back for season 24 is remarkable. There's nothing left to prove, and yet here he is.

Season tips off October 20. 76ers at Knicks. MSG. LeBron on the road, opening night, in New York.

This is going to be something. 👑

stories.title: Stephen Curry Extension — 7 Days to August 29 Window — Tier 2

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
7 days until Stephen Curry can sign his Warriors extension.

GM Dunleavy: "He really, really wants to finish his career as a Warrior."

August 29. The countdown is on. ⏰

#Warriors #NBA #StephCurry

facebook.long_form:
Window: 4:00 PM ET

One week.

Seven days from today — August 29 — Stephen Curry becomes eligible to sign a contract extension with the Golden State Warriors.

Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. isn't worried. "He really, really wants to win and he wants to finish his career as a Warrior," Dunleavy said. "I don't think that changes tomorrow, August 29th, start of the season, middle of the season..."

The available max is 2 years, $136.7 million. But reports suggest Curry might prefer a shorter structure — potentially 1 year around $62.6 million — giving both sides more flexibility heading into 2027-28.

The context matters: the Warriors finished 37-45 last season and couldn't land LeBron, Giannis, Jaylen Brown, or Anthony Davis in the offseason. If Curry signs short-term, it could open the door for one more major roster move.

If he doesn't sign an extension at all? He becomes a free agent for the first time in his career in 2027. The FIRST time. At 39 years old.

But Dunleavy says he's not worried. And for what it's worth — neither are most Warriors fans.

The countdown is on. August 29. ⏰

article.headline: Seven Days Until Steph Curry's Extension Window Opens — and Warriors Aren't Worried

stories.title: DeMar DeRozan Signs With Denver Nuggets — Tier 2

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
DeMar DeRozan is going to Denver.

Six-time All-Star signs a 1-year, $3.9M deal with the Nuggets — joining Jokic and Murray as a midrange playmaker.

Denver quietly stacking up again. 🏔️

#Nuggets #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 7:00 PM ET

The Denver Nuggets just added another dangerous piece.

Six-time All-Star DeMar DeRozan has agreed to a 1-year, $3.88 million veteran minimum deal with Denver — joining Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray, and a Nuggets squad quietly building for another title run.

DeRozan is 37 years old and coming off a season where he averaged 18.4 points in 77 games for the Sacramento Kings. He brings exactly what Denver needs: a reliable midrange scorer, a veteran ball-handler, and a calming presence next to the two-time MVP.

He had offers from the Heat, Wizards, and Pelicans. He chose Denver — because he wants to compete.

This is the Nuggets' way: they don't make splashy signings, they make smart ones. Jokic and Murray as the foundation, and smart veteran acquisitions stacked around them.

DeRozan as a third option in crunch time, running pick-and-rolls with Jokic? That's a nightmare for opposing defenses.

The Nuggets are quietly dangerous again. Don't sleep on them. 🏔️
